newsitem.title: UK: Northwest to act on no-show cargo agents.
newsitem.headline: Northwest to act on no-show cargo agents.

text.p: Northwest Airlines will take tough action in future against forwarders or shippers which fail to use pre-booked space, its Atlantic division cargo director Brian Mutton told Reuters.
He said that in future, persistent "no-show" offenders could well find their cargo booked with Northwest being handled on a "stand-by" basis only.
"We are currently looking into this problem and we will definitely be doing something about it," said Mutton.
"Some people who regularly abuse the system may well find, for example, shipments urgently required for a U.S. production line remaining on the ground on stand-by," he added.
"That would leave them with egg on their faces and it will also get the message across that they can't get away with this behaviour," he said.
Mutton welcomed the recent initiatives of Air Canada, Air Hong Kong and Emirates to impose penalties on cargo agents and shippers which regularly fail to take up booked space allocations.
"I think this is a good idea. If an agent makes a booking then he should pay for the space," he said.
But while he said he would look into the possibility of Northwest also introducing fines for "no-show" agents and shippers, he warned there was no guarantee the offenders would pay them.
This is why he said he at present preferred to consider using the option of placing on stand-by cargo provided by forwarders and agents with a record of failing to deliver shipments as booked.
"But something must be done. At five to five on Monday afternoon, we got a call from an agent in the UK cancelling a two-tonne shipment booked for Detroit the next day," he said.
"This left us with a big, last minute space filling problem. This particular agent has done the same in the past. He and others like him are abusing the system all the time," stated Mutton.

He felt that airlines should stand together in order to reduce "no-shows" and felt that the UK Air Freight Forum -- a tripartite talking shop amongst carriers, forwarders and shippers set up last year -- might be the best vehicle to achieve this aim.
